rules.sentence: The anatomy of the ulnar nerve makes it susceptible to compression.
Entrapment at the elbow can be caused by leaning on the elbow for prolonged periods, medial epicondyle fractures, chronic subluxation, arthritis within the ulnar groove, and bony deformity.
Approximately 75% of medial epicondylar fractures occur in male pediatric patients, with 10% to 15% of those resulting in ulnar nerve dysfunction.[4]
Less commonly, ulnar nerve entrapment can also occur at the wrist in the Guyon canal, formed by the pisiform and hook of the hamate.
The most common causes of ulnar neuropathy at the wrist are repetitive trauma and ganglion cysts.[5]
About 30 to 45% of all cases of Guyon syndrome are due to ganglion cysts.[6]
Ulnar nerve compression at the wrist is commonly seen in bikers due to excess pressure from handlebars and desk workers due to prolonged periods of typing.[7]
